name: Kalshi BTC pair-cost state
description: Kalshi quotes a single binary YES book. Locking a one-dollar payout means buying YES at yes_ask and buying NO at no_ask, where no_ask equals one minus yes_bid (the NO purchase crosses the other side of the same book), so pair_cost = yes_ask + no_ask - 1 = yes_ask - yes_bid, the YES spread (pair-locking on one binary book is spread capture). fee_adjusted_pair_cost adds the taker fee on both legs. The fee model is Kalshi's official fee schedule effective 2026-07-07: taker fee per contract = fee_rate * P * (1 - P) rounded up to the fee_alignment increment. The BTC series take the general schedule. This is the conservative taker-taker case (both legs crossing); resting one side pays the maker rate, which defaults to zero for the BTC series under the current schedule, so taker-taker is the worst case. There is no settlement fee, so holding both sides to expiry costs exactly the two entry fees. state is locked_profit when fee_adjusted_pair_cost is negative, premium when it exceeds premium_threshold, and fair otherwise. A missing outcome ask is a defined not-ready state. fee_rate defaults to 0.07, fee_alignment defaults to 0.01 (the non-direct member increment; the direct-member tier is 0.0001), and premium_threshold defaults to 0.01. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
